papers.title_en: RBGA: Residual-Budget Guide Arbitration for Offline-to-Online Safe Reinforcement Learning in Dexterous Manipulation
papers.authors: Zongyou Yu, Ao Zhou, Xiongbo Shi, Jiayi Guan, Shihang Du, Xudong Zhang, Shangding Gu, Junqiao Zhao, Hanli Wang, Guang Chen
papers.evidence: 显式考虑安全预算的离线到在线安全约束强化学习
papers.tldr: 灵巧操作需借助离线数据快速习得技能，并在真实部署中保障安全，离线到在线安全强化学习（O2O safe RL）是可行路径。现有方法未显式考虑单回合已消耗的安全预算，早期成本过高会压缩后续探索与策略改进空间。RBGA跟踪剩余回合安全预算，逐步比较离线引导与在线动作的cost-to-go估计，据此仲裁动作选择。实验显示其能在保持强安全性的同时实现在线策略改进，为安全预算感知的O2O安全RL提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Dexterous manipulation requires robots to leverage existing datasets for rapid skill acquisition while maintaining safety during real-world deployment to prevent damage to the robot or its surroundings. Offline-to-online safe reinforcement learning (O2O safe RL) provides a promising solution for this problem by leveraging prior experience for online improvement under safety constraints, thereby mitigating the sample inefficiency and exploration risk of learning safe policies from scratch. However, existing O2O safe RL approaches do not explicitly account for the safety budget already consumed when making decisions within an episode. Excessive cost incurred early can therefore leave little room for subsequent exploration and policy improvement. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{R}esidual-\textbf{B}udget \textbf{G}uide \textbf{A}rbitration (RBGA), an algorithm that explicitly tracks the remaining episode safety budget and uses it to adaptively select between offline guidance and the evolving online policy. At each step, RBGA compares the cost-to-go estimates of the guide and online actions against the remaining budget, enabling step-wise action arbitration throughout the episode. We provide theoretical analysis characterizing the safety implications of residual-budget-based selection and its effect on guide-assisted exploration. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RBGA enables effective online policy improvement while maintaining strong safety performance. Our code is available at this \href{https://github.com/sii-pilab}{link}.

papers.title_en: Tikhonov-Regularized Dynamics and Inexact Algorithms for Nonlinear Saddle-Point Problems
papers.evidence: 凸-凹鞍点问题的正则化原始-对偶动力学求解
papers.tldr: 针对光滑非线性凸-凹鞍点问题，构建含α/t阻尼、Hessian驱动项与c/t^2 Tikhonov正则的二阶原始-对偶动力系统；借助Lyapunov函数证明轨迹强收敛至最小范数鞍点，gap与速度分别达o(t^-2)、o(t^-1)；进而设计带可计算相对残差准则的不精确算法，获得序列强收敛及o(k^-2) gap率；数值实验验证最小范数选择并比较性能。
papers.abstract_en: In this paper, we study a Tikhonov-regularized second-order primal--dual dynamical system for smooth nonlinear convex--concave saddle-point problems in real Hilbert spaces. The dynamical system incorporates a vanishing damping coefficient $α/t$, a Hessian-driven term, and a critical Tikhonov regularization coefficient $c/t^2$. By constructing suitable Lyapunov functions, we establish strong convergence to the minimum-norm saddle point and fast convergence rates under the same parameter conditions, without imposing any eventual inside/outside-ball condition. Specifically, the primal--dual trajectory converges strongly to the minimum-norm saddle point, while the primal--dual gap and the velocity norm decay at rates $o(t^{-2})$ and $o(t^{-1})$, respectively. Furthermore, we propose an inexact primal--dual algorithm with a computable relative residual criterion and prove strong convergence of the generated sequence to the same minimum-norm saddle point, together with an $o(k^{-2})$ convergence rate for the primal--dual gap. Finally, numerical experiments on nonlinear and bilinear problems of different dimensions illustrate the minimum-norm selection property and compare the performance of the proposed dynamical system and algorithm with related methods.

papers.title_en: A New Perspective on Optimal Power Flow: From Control Theory to Numerical Optimization
papers.authors: Yeming Xu, Qi Liu, Liping Zhang, Huanshui Zhang, Minyue Fu
papers.evidence: 借助最大值原理将最优潮流重构为最优控制问题
papers.tldr: 最优潮流是含非线性约束的非凸优化问题，现有方法常难获全局最优且难以系统发现多个局部解。本文用罚函数与拉格朗日乘子处理约束，将OPF重构为最优控制问题，并借助最大值原理建立联系。作者提出数值算法求解该控制问题，使状态轨迹快速稳定收敛，并通过设计初始控制序列找到多个解、跳出局部解。仿真验证了该方法在非凸问题多解辨识上的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: The optimal power flow (OPF) problem is a classical non-convex optimization problem with nonlinear constraints and multiple potential solutions. Existing methods often fail to find the global optimal solution, motivating the development of a method to identify multiple local solutions. This paper applies the optimal control principle to solve the OPF problem, aiming to systematically explore all feasible solutions within a single run. We first handle the constraints in the OPF problem using the penalty method and the Lagrange multiplier, and then reformulate it as an optimal control problem. The connection between the two problems is established by the maximum principle. Moreover, a numerical algorithm is proposed to solve this optimal control problem. The state trajectory of the system can rapidly and stably converge to the solution of the OPF problem. By designing the initial control sequence, the proposed method can successfully find multiple solutions and escape local solutions. Finally, simulations were conducted on several representative test systems to validate the potential of the proposed method in identifying multiple solutions for non-convex problems.

papers.title_en: Escaping Path Mirages in Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Junhyeon Bae, Jaebak Hwang, Gwanwoo Choi, Minung Kim, Seungyul Han
papers.evidence: 离线目标条件强化学习中的价值估计误差与策略优化
papers.tldr: 离线目标条件强化学习在随机长时程任务中受价值误差累积困扰，智能体易把数据中偶然成功的轨迹误判为可行路径，形成“路径海市蜃楼”。为此，作者提出分支感知图规划 BGP：将高方差点识别为图节点，并用分段学习构建目标条件边，避开不可靠分支、降低路径随机性。在多个 OGBench 任务上，BGP 显著优于先前最先进的离线目标条件 RL 方法，表明其能在高随机长时程环境中实现可靠目标到达。
papers.abstract_en: Offline goal-conditioned reinforcement learning remains challenging in stochastic long-horizon settings, where compounding value estimation errors hinder reliable goal reaching. While prior methods have sought to address this challenge through various approaches, a key challenge remains path mirage, where agents overcommit to spuriously successful trajectories in offline datasets induced by stochasticity, often leading to failure on difficult tasks. To address this issue, we propose Branch-aware Graph Planning (BGP), which captures stochastic branching structures by identifying high-variability points as graph nodes and designing goal-conditioned edges with segmented learning to avoid unreliable branches and reduce unnecessary stochasticity along paths. As a result, BGP enables reliable goal reaching even in highly stochastic long-horizon environments, and experiments on diverse OGBench tasks show that it substantially outperforms prior state-of-the-art offline goal-conditioned RL methods. Our implementation is available at https://umlic.github.io/papers/BGP/.
